$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./b  # chain-b-nooutputs
    export/quoted: import rejects the export.
        evaluate: Does what the case's evaluate/ tree says, from the stage it consumes.
        The cell of the lift import, on evaluate's path, has a problem, which that cell reports, in the package that owns it. A normal run reads the product and the outcome the archive commits for import, so this cell runs nothing.
        Fix what import's cell reports. An update writes nothing for the cell of the lift import, on evaluate's path, nor for this cell.
    export/quoted: import rejects the export.
        list: Lists the files of the script's input view, with their bytes.
        The cell of the lift import, on list's path, has a problem, which that cell reports, in the package that owns it. A normal run reads the product and the outcome the archive commits for import, so this cell runs nothing.
        Fix what import's cell reports. An update writes nothing for the cell of the lift import, on list's path, nor for this cell.

$ go test  # chain-a
    the registries that own or use the lift import differ in outputs:
          outputs:
            .: error.txt "Why the importer rejects the export."
            ./b: none
        Every package that owns or uses a lift registers one declaration of it: a package that only uses a bytes lift tells by its own declaration whether an update writes the lift's cell, and so the cells past it. Declare the lift once, in a package the others import, and register that declaration. If they register one declaration already, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
    export/quoted: parse is blocked: testdata/export/quoted.txtar, out/import/outcome, records the lift import's outcome as "rejected".
